comment: Shared pairing-URL conformance cases, fixture-pinned across the desktop TS reference (src/shared/remote/pairingUrl.ts), iOS (ios/App/App/Protocol/PairingURL.swift), and Android (android/.../protocol/PairingUrl.kt). Every asserted case MUST produce the identical result on all three platforms; the desktop TS implementation is canonical. Cases whose behavior legitimately differs per platform live in documentedDifferences and are pinned by native-only or desktop-only tests instead. Duplicate query/fragment parameters resolve to the FIRST occurrence everywhere (URLSearchParams.get / queryItems first(where:) / first-wins map).

parseParts.name: direct desktop link with fragment token
surrounding whitespace is trimmed before parsing
hosted link with percent-encoded host parameter
userinfo in authority must not shadow the fragment credential
fragment credential wins over a query credential
duplicate fragment tokens resolve to the first occurrence
duplicate host parameters resolve to the first occurrence
hosted link without any credential is unusable
relative link without a scheme is unusable

normalizeEndpoint.name: desktop link strips the credential fragment
hosted link follows the encoded host parameter
host parameter can itself carry an app suffix
pair suffix with trailing slash is stripped
relay base path is preserved while the suffix is stripped
vite dev port rewrites to the remote-access port
bare scheme without a host is invalid

cleartextLanUrl.name: plain http LAN endpoint is cleartext
dns hostname over http is cleartext
ipv4 loopback is not cleartext LAN
bracketed ipv6 loopback is not cleartext LAN
subdomains under localhost are not cleartext LAN
android emulator host alias is treated as a normal lan host

documentedDifferences.area: parseParts: token in the query of an http(s) link
documentedDifferences.behavior: iOS and Android fall back to a query credential when the fragment is absent; the desktop reference requires the #token fragment and returns null.
documentedDifferences.reason: Mobile deep-link plumbing (QR re-encoding, intent/app-router round trips) can drop URL fragments, so the natives accept the query fallback; desktop links are always built by the host with a fragment. Pinned natively by PairingUrlTest.parseTokenFromQueryAsFallback and the iOS query-token tests.

documentedDifferences.behavior: Natives parse poracode://pair?host=…&token=… (fragment or query credential); the desktop reference returns null because the custom scheme never reaches desktop code.
documentedDifferences.reason: The custom scheme is a mobile-only deep-link surface. Routing above the shared parse (parseDeepLink / validatedPairingCandidate) is pinned by native-only tests (PairingIntentDecisionsTest, iOS candidate tests).

documentedDifferences.area: loopback scope for the cleartext gate
documentedDifferences.behavior: Android additionally treats the whole 127.0.0.0/8 range as loopback in this classifier; desktop and iOS pin the exact host set localhost/127.0.0.1/::1/[::1] plus *.localhost.
documentedDifferences.reason: On a phone, a 127.x address is the phone itself, so rejecting it as an endpoint is strictly safer. Separately, at a deeper layer, Android's transport cleartext gate only dials private/loopback addresses and knows the 10.0.2.2 emulator alias (CleartextPolicy/LocalNetworkAccess via isPrivateOrLoopbackHostname) — that is transport enforcement, not this URL classifier, which is exactly why http://10.0.2.2 asserts cleartext:true above on all platforms.

documentedDifferences.behavior: Natives require http/https and reject other schemes; the desktop normalizer accepts any parsable URL scheme.
documentedDifferences.reason: The mobile input is a security gate for network endpoints; the desktop paste box only normalizes text before further validation happens elsewhere.

documentedDifferences.behavior: Desktop URLSearchParams and Android URLDecoder decode '+' as a space; iOS URLComponents leaves it literal.
documentedDifferences.reason: Pairing credentials are base64url (no '+', '/') and endpoint hosts are percent-encoded, so no canonical claim is needed; avoid '+' in fixture-asserted values.
